front: What was the Industrial Conciliation Act of 1934?
back: A law that defined 'employee' so as to exclude Africans, denying African unions the right to bargain.

front: What was the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland?
back: A union of Southern Rhodesia, Northern Rhodesia and Nyasaland (1953-63), dominated by white settlers.

front: Which strikes showed the power of African workers in the 1940s?
back: The railway strike of 1945 and the general strike of 1948.

front: What was the City Youth League?
back: An organisation formed in 1955 in Salisbury that led the 1956 bus boycott and merged into Congress in 1957.

Why did unionism give way to mass nationalism?
back: Unions were legally weak and the main grievances (land, the vote) were political; the Federation and decolonisation elsewhere also pushed Africans towards parties.

front: How did the Federation help nationalism grow?
back: It strengthened white control and offered only 'partnership' in name, so Africans turned to political organisation.

front: What did the 1956 bus boycott show?
back: That mass action could win concessions, as the fare rise was reduced.
